## **Basics**

**R is free**

* Download R from <https://cran.r-project.org>

- Install RStudio IDE (an R Integrated Development Environment tool)

http://www.rstudio.com/products/rstudio/download

**R is a function language**

* All commands in R are regarded as functions.  
+ \texttt{plot(x, y)} produces a scatter plot of \texttt{x} vs. \texttt{y}. 

+ Help is also a function. To obtain help on the function plot use help(plot). To obtain general help use help(), i.e.use the function help with a null argument. 

+ To end a session in R use the function quit().

**R is an object orientated language**

* All entities in R are objects. This includes vectors, matrices, data arrays, graphs, functions, and results of an analysis.

**Getting Help in R**

\begin{itemize}
\item documentation on “mean”\\
\
– ?mean\\
– help(mean)

\item returns a character vector giving the names of all
objects in the search list matching\\
– apropos('mean')

\end{itemize}

-------------------

**Basics- Vectors**

To create a vector of numbers, we use the function \texttt{c()}

```{r}
x <- c(1,3,2,5) 
x
```

The length of a vector is found using the \texttt{length()} function.

```{r}
length(x)
```


---------------------

**Descriptive statistics on Vectors**

- mean 

```{r}
mean(x)
```

- meadian  

```{r}
median(x)
```

- min 
```{r} 
min(x)

```

-------------------

**Random Sampling**


```{r rsamp}
big_vector <- 1:10000
x1=sample(big_vector, 100)
x1

```

--------------

**Assemenment**

- Challenge 1: For x1, find the

(i) maximun value

(ii) median value

(iii) the 70th percentile value

--------------------

**Answers**

```{r rsamp1}
max(x1)
median(x1)
quantile(x1, 0.7)
```

------------------

**Vector Operations**

1. Summary
```{r}
summary(x)

```

2. Take a subset of the data

```{r}
x[1:3]
```

3. Scalar operation on the subset

```{r}
x[1:3]/100
```

4. **Scalar operation on the subset**


```{r}
x[1:2]+ x[4:5]

```

-------------

**PLotting Vectors**


```{r}
plot(x1)
```

----------------

**Properties of Plot**

```{r, warning=FALSE}
par(mfrow=c(1,2))
plot(x1,pch=20,col="red")
plot(x1,pch=20,col="blue", typle ="l")

```
---------------

**Matrices**

To create a matrix of numbers, we use the function \texttt{matrix()}

```{r}
y<- matrix(c(1,2,3,4), 2, 2)
y
```
---------------


Take the square-root of each element of the matrix \texttt{y}

```{r}
sqrt(y)
```

-----------

## **Powers**

Square each element of the matrix \texttt{y}
```{r}
y^2
```

The square of the matrix \texttt{y}
```{r}
y%*%y
```

**Creating a Vector by Sequence**

Sequence vectors can be created in several ways.

```{r}
seq(1,10, 1)
seq(1,10, length=10)
seq(1,10)
1:10
```

---------------

**More sequence vectors**

More sequences

```{r}
seq(1,10, 2)
seq(1,10, length=5)
rep(1,4)
rep(1:4, 3)
```

**Basics**

Matrices

```{r}
diag(3)
matrix(1,3,4)
```

-----------

**Basics**

More matrices

```{r}
matrix(1:4, 3, 4, byrow=TRUE)
outer(1:3, 1:3, "+")/2
```

 **Binding Vectors and Matrices**

Binding vectors into matrices

```{r}
x <- c(1,2,3)
y <- seq(4,6)
rbind(x,y)
cbind(x,y)
```

**Data Frames**


```{r}
subjects <- c('Jim','Jack','Joe','Mary','Jean')
sex <- c('M', 'M', 'M', 'F', 'F')
score <- c(85,90,75,100,70)
D2 <- data.frame(subjects,sex,score)
D2
```

----------------

**Operations on Data Frames**

1. Extracting a values

```{r}
D2$score
mean(D2$score)
with(D2, mean(score))
```

------------------

**Creating a new variable in data frame**

Adding a new variable

```{r}
D2$letter<-c('B', 'A', 'C', 'A', 'C')
D2
```

**Reading Data** 

- Read the Botswana average monthly temperature data into $R$.

```{r, warning=F, message=F}
library(readr)
BW <- read_csv("C:/Users/zidanac/OneDrive - biust.ac.bw/BIUST/STAT 303 Linear regression/R lectures/BWtemp.csv")
head(BW, 4)
```
----------------

**Data Importing**


```{r dataimp}
library(readr)
# import white space delimited files
all_data <- read_table(file = "C:/Users/zidanac/OneDrive - biust.ac.bw/BIUST/STAT 303 Linear regression/R lectures/BWtemp.csv", col_names = TRUE)

# import comma delimited files
all_data <- read_csv(file = "C:/Users/zidanac/OneDrive - biust.ac.bw/BIUST/STAT 303 Linear regression/R lectures/BWtemp.csv")

# import tab delimited files
all_data <- read_delim(file = "C:/Users/zidanac/OneDrive - biust.ac.bw/BIUST/STAT 303 Linear regression/R lectures/BWtemp.csv", delim = "\t")

# or use
all_data <- read_tsv(file = "C:/Users/zidanac/OneDrive - biust.ac.bw/BIUST/STAT 303 Linear regression/R lectures/BWtemp.csv")

```

**Working with Data** 

Drop a variable
```{r}
BW$Country <- NULL
head(BW)
```

-------------------


```{r}
str(BW)

```

-----------------

**Working with Data** 

- Calculate the average annual temperature

```{r}
BW.y <- aggregate(Temperature ~ Year, data=BW, mean)
head(BW.y, 3)
BW.y <- with(BW, tapply(Temperature, Year, mean))
head(BW.y, 3)
```

-------------------------

**Working with Data** 

Calculate the average of all variables
```{r}
colMeans(BW)
BW.m <- as.matrix(BW)
apply(BW.m, 2, mean)
```

----------------------

**Working with Dataframes** 

Referencing values in a matrix
```{r}
BW.m[1,2]
BW.m[1:3,1:2]
```

---

```{r}
BW.m[2,]
BW.m[2,c(1,3)]
BW.m[2,-1]
```

**Installing and Loading Packages**

- to install packages u=you ned to write the following command:*install.packages("ggplot2")*

- Loading a package in the workpace: *library(ggplot2)*

- load data in the workspace: 


```{r loadpack, warning=FALSE, message=F}
library(ggplot2)
## Use and load data in work space
data("txhousing")
data("mpg")
```

# Graphics

**Enter Data**


```{r data1}
## House Price
HP = c(245,312,279,308,199,219,405,324,319,255)
##size of house
X=c(1400,1600,1700,1875,1100,1550,2350,2450,1425,1700) 
df1 = as.data.frame(cbind(X, HP))
```

------------------------

**Histogram of House Price**

```{r}
with(df1, hist(HP))
```


---------------------------

 **Scatter Plot  basis**

```{r}
with(df1, plot(X, HP))
```

------------------

**Graphics with dplyr and ggplot2

```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
df1%>%
  ggplot(aes(X, HP))+
  geom_point()+theme_bw()
  
```

-------------------------------

**Boxplot Graphics**

- A comparison boxplot of Month vs. Temperature.

```{r}
with(BW, boxplot(Temperature ~ Month))
```

**Functions in R**



----------------------

**Evaluating Functions in R**

```{r ffunction}
f1=function(x){
  sin (x^2)*cos(sqrt(x^4+3)-x^2)-x +1
  }
x=seq(-3, 3, by = 0.1)
y1= f1(x)
plot(x,y1)

```
